instruction: Navigate to en.wikipedia.org and search for 'Spider-Man'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent encountered 'Access Denied' on kohls.com. Navigated to Amazon, searched 'Spider-Man toys for kids', and sorted by 'Price: Low to High'. Task scored 0 because evaluator required kohls.com-specific elements.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome address bar, search products on Amazon, use sort dropdowns, handle blocked sites by navigating elsewhere
metadata.failure_analysis: Kohls.com returned Access Denied. Model adapted by going to Amazon, but evaluator checks kohls.com-specific HTML breadcrumbs and sort selector.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests basic navigation and search on a different, reliably accessible website. Wikipedia is unlikely to block access. Keeps the Spider-Man theme from the original task.
metadata.explanation: Uses is_expected_url_pattern_match to verify the URL contains wikipedia.org and Spider-Man, confirming successful navigation and search.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter active_url_from_accessTree correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL, which is the right state to verify navigation and search.
Metric is_expected_url_pattern_match correctly receives the rules dict with expected patterns and checks all patterns against the URL via re.search.
Both instruction requirements (navigate to wikipedia.org, search for Spider-Man) are covered by the two regex patterns.

Minor issue: Instruction specifies 'en.wikipedia.org' but pattern 'wikipedia\.org' would also match other language subdomains (fr, de, etc.). Pattern should be 'en\.wikipedia\.org' for precise verification.
Data flow is correct: getter returns URL string, metric iterates patterns and returns 1.0 only if all patterns match.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change first pattern from 'wikipedia\\.org' to 'en\\.wikipedia\\.org' to enforce the specific subdomain mentioned in the instruction.
